title: Harden Shiki for safe self-hosted / team / production repository use
outcome: Shiki can be safely used as a GitHub-first control plane and repository template without known contract contradictions, unsafe bootstrap behavior, weak MergeGate enforcement, race-prone state handling, or undocumented operational gaps.
completion_conditions: All P0, P1, and P2 remediation checklist items from GitHub Issue #30 are complete or Guardian-approved as non-goals.
Each checked item links to durable evidence: PR, commit, test output, CI run, CCA verdict, MergeGate result, review, ledger entry, or documented Guardian decision.
Validation, Python compile, all Shiki contract tests, CCA, MergeGate, review, and ledger evidence pass for each task PR.
Final Goal completion judgment records why Shiki is safe enough for self-hosted, team, and production repository use.
non_goals: Do not add unrelated product features.
Do not rewrite the whole repository unless a bounded task proves that a smaller change cannot satisfy acceptance.
Do not make API-key Codex automation the default path.
Do not weaken CCA, MergeGate, review, ledger, or Guardian concepts.
acceptance_evidence: Each task has a PR using the Shiki PR template.
Each task PR has passing validation and test output.
Each task PR has CCA complete verdict and MergeGate pass evidence.
Ledger entries record work, checks, review, CCA, MergeGate, repairs, and completion judgment.

grill_with_docs.source: GitHub Issue #30 and attached external review
grill_with_docs.summary: External review identified contract drift, bootstrap safety risks, MergeGate/review enforcement gaps, race-prone state handling, mutable evidence concerns, maintainability debt, packaging gaps, and missing adversarial tests. This plan decomposes remediation into bounded Shiki task PRs.

tasks.title: Normalize Shiki contracts and source-of-truth
tasks.scope: Align authority order, CCA schema paths, canonical constants, and validator coverage across contracts, runtime wrappers, workflows, docs, and skills.
non_goals: Do not alter runtime behavior except to enforce corrected contracts.
acceptance_checks: Authority order is canonical and consistent across all contract surfaces.
All obsolete CCA schema references are replaced or rejected by validation.
Canonical contract constants are centralized for schema paths, required checks, runtime names, source-of-truth order, and state directories.
Validator detects authority-order and CCA-schema-path drift.
Regression tests cover authority-order drift and obsolete CCA schema path cases.

tasks.title: Make bootstrap and init safe by default
tasks.scope: Remove dangerous default side effects from bootstrap/init, including silent origin rewrite, broad git staging, warning-only branch protection failure, and warning-only required secret failure.
non_goals: Do not remove advanced setup flows; gate them behind explicit flags.
acceptance_checks: Existing origin mismatch fails or requires explicit adoption.
Setup commits stage only Shiki-owned manifest files.
Required branch protection failure returns non-zero.
Required missing CCA secret returns non-zero.
Tests cover unsafe bootstrap cases.

tasks.title: Enforce MergeGate, review, branch protection, and Guardian rules
tasks.scope: Make required checks single-source, ensure required_review is enforced by GitHub branch protection, separate advisory AI review from blocking review, and make Guardian approval machine-readable.
non_goals: Do not weaken CCA or MergeGate to make PRs easier to merge.
acceptance_checks: Required checks are defined once and validated against workflow job names.
required_review true maps to at least one enforced approval.
Advisory AI review cannot satisfy blocking review.
Guardian approvals are checked through configured users or teams.
MergeGate blocks missing CCA, review, ledger, required checks, and Guardian evidence.

tasks.title: Fix state concurrency, IDs, locks, and evidence integrity
tasks.scope: Replace race-prone ID allocation, add safe state write semantics, unify lock matching, and prevent forged PR-local evidence from satisfying MergeGate.
non_goals: Do not introduce an external database unless justified by ADR.
acceptance_checks: ID allocation is collision-resistant or based on GitHub identifiers.
State writes are atomic or safely retried.
Dispatch and MergeGate use the same lock matcher.
Lock matcher handles exact, glob, prefix, and documented semantic overlap.
Tests cover collisions, lock conflicts, and forged evidence.

tasks.title: Add manifest and align .shiki layout
tasks.scope: Define Shiki-owned files, generated files, state directories, commit behavior, and local-only runtime files through a manifest and align README, code, and validators.
non_goals: Do not redesign the entire state model in this task.
acceptance_checks: .shiki manifest or equivalent exists.
.shiki README, actual tree, code constants, and validators agree.
Required empty directories are preserved or generated intentionally.
CI fails on layout drift.

tasks.title: Harden validators and workflow checks
tasks.scope: Move brittle string checks toward structured validation, add schema/workflow validation tests, and add actionlint/shellcheck or document why not.
non_goals: Do not add heavyweight dependencies to the bootstrap shim unless isolated.
acceptance_checks: Workflow validation is structured where practical.
Schema validation strategy is explicit and tested.
Validator false-positive and false-negative cases are covered.
actionlint/shellcheck are integrated or rejected with durable rationale.

tasks.title: Split architecture and define runtime/provider adapters
tasks.scope: Refactor the monolithic CLI/control-plane script into maintainable modules while preserving bootstrap behavior and defining runtime/provider extension points.
non_goals: Do not change user-facing commands unless compatibility is preserved or migration is documented.
dependencies: Make bootstrap and init safe by default
acceptance_checks: Bootstrap shim remains usable.
Config, GitHub, contracts, state, MergeGate, and runtime logic are separated.
Runtime registry or adapter contract exists.
GitHub host/protocol/provider assumptions are configurable.
doctor verifies operational readiness.

tasks.title: Strengthen governance and evidence model
tasks.scope: Make Guardian approval, CCA verdict evidence, ledger integrity, and mirror/generated/cache distinctions machine-checkable.
non_goals: Do not require a paid external service.
dependencies: Enforce MergeGate, review, branch protection, and Guardian rules
Fix state concurrency, IDs, locks, and evidence integrity
acceptance_checks: Guardian approvers are configured as users or teams.
CCA verdict evidence cannot be forged by PR file edits alone.
Ledger evidence has hash/check/artifact/signature cross-reference or documented equivalent.
Mirror, generated, cache, and local-only state are documented and validated.
Tests cover forged, stale, and missing governance evidence.

tasks.title: Add distribution and onboarding documentation
tasks.scope: Add root README, license/security/contribution docs, install/upgrade/rollback docs, release/versioning strategy, and clarify platform-vs-template boundaries.
non_goals: Do not publish a release until P0 and P1 gates pass.
dependencies: Make bootstrap and init safe by default
Split architecture and define runtime/provider adapters
acceptance_checks: Root onboarding docs exist.
Security and contribution policy exist.
Install, upgrade, rollback, and migration are documented.
Versioning and release strategy are documented or implemented.
Platform runtime and target template responsibilities are clear.

tasks.title: Add adversarial and regression test suite
tasks.scope: Add tests for malicious PR mutation, fork PR limitations, duplicate IDs, lock conflicts, missing CCA, branch protection failure, schema drift, required check drift, and repair loop limits.
non_goals: Do not fake passing tests by weakening validation.
dependencies: Make bootstrap and init safe by default
Enforce MergeGate, review, branch protection, and Guardian rules
Fix state concurrency, IDs, locks, and evidence integrity
acceptance_checks: All P2.3 adversarial tests exist.
Tests run in CI.
Tests fail against representative broken fixtures.
Repair loop limit and repair packet content are tested.
